name: Historic Centre (Sintra-Vila)
tagline: Fairytale old town by the palace
description: The romantic old village around the National Palace with its twin chimneys, winding cobbled lanes, cafes and craft shops. The most scenic and visited base, close to the tourist bus loop for the hilltop palaces, though very crowded by day and steep throughout.
bestFor: Visitors wanting the classic Sintra setting near palaces and cafes

name: Estefania
tagline: Practical quarter near the train station
description: The area around Sintra's train station, more modern and residential than the old village. Home to everyday shops, restaurants, the town hall and services, it offers direct rail links to Lisbon and easier parking, making it a practical base for longer stays.
bestFor: Commuters and nomads wanting rail access and daily conveniences

name: Sao Pedro de Penaferrim
tagline: Village of the famous monthly market
description: A traditional village just southeast of the center, known for its large Sunday and second-Sunday market and local tascas. More residential and Portuguese in feel, with restaurants popular among locals, it gives a quieter, more affordable base a short ride from Sintra-Vila.
bestFor: Travellers wanting local eateries, markets and value outside the crowds

name: Serra de Sintra (near Pena)
description: The wooded hillsides climbing toward Pena Palace and the Moorish Castle, dotted with quintas, guesthouses and estates amid dense green forest. Peaceful and dramatic with cool microclimate and misty mornings, it suits those wanting nature and quiet over convenience.
bestFor: Nature seekers wanting quiet forest stays near hilltop palaces
